title: Austin Infrastructure and Vital Records Updates
summary:
• **Electric and Water Services Expansion** – The city approved petitions to extend electric light wires to the Hyde Park area and install a new water main in Block 23, delegating both projects to the Water & Light Commission for planning and implementation.

• **Street Improvements and Bridge Construction** – Citizens seeking street work on West 8th and Guadalupe streets were required to contribute $500 toward costs, with the city covering the rest. Additionally, the city approved construction of a concrete bridge across Shoal Creek on West Avenue.

• **Vital Statistics Records Law Passed** – The council unanimously passed an ordinance requiring official record-keeping of births and vital statistics throughout Austin, establishing penalties for non-compliance.

• **City Expansion** – The council approved a petition from Glenwood addition residents to annex their neighborhood into Austin's city limits, subject to certain conditions.

• **Water & Light Leadership Changes** – Following the death of board president Geo T. Hume and a commissioner's resignation, the council elected James Belger and John Newland to fill the two vacant positions on the Water & Light Commission.

Report of Special
Committee on the Death
Geo T Hume
Whereas,the death of Geo T Hume,President of the Water and Light Board of the City of
Austin,has been suddenly cut off in the midst of a most useful life,and while he was in
the full vigor of manhood, And Whereas,his death while so young and promising in
usefulness to the City,is a mystery that human intelligence cannot comprehend,and
Whereas,some expression of the loss of so valuable a citizen ,and so capabal an
official,is becoming and appropriate by the municipal body, so intimately connected with
the Water and Light Commission,therefore, Be it resolved,that in the death of Geo T
Hume,not only the Commission of which he was President,but the whole community,has
suffered a loss that it will be difficult to remedy,because of his active intelligence in
the administration of his official position,and because of his high and unquestioned
integrity,and the confidence and trust reposed in him by this body,as well as the entire
population of the City,and because of the promise of his future usefulness,as an Official
and Citizen.
Resolved,That we desire to express our esteem for him as a man and official,and our deep
regret at his death,in the fullness of his man-hood,and be it further, Resolved,That we
tender his bereaved family,our sympathy and condo-lence ,and offer to them the
consolationef the assurance of his integrity and his very unquestionedhonorable life,and
Resolved further,that these resolutions,be filed in archives of this body,and a minute be
made of them,in the records of the Council,and that that they be published in the
newspapers of the VCity,and that a copy be sent to his family,under the seal of the City
of Austin,Texas . C W Moore
